transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

I’m here because... well, for the past year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. I'm a phlebotomist, so I know what I'm looking at. But no matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine, I know the chart doesn’t match what I saw. It’s just... it's really wearing me down trying to get someone to listen to me about it.
Do you believe that someone in the clinic system is intentionally altering or withholding your father’s lab results on purpose, or do you think it might be a mistake or misunderstanding?

It’s definitely on purpose. I mean, like I was just saying, I’ve been trying to prove this for a whole year now. If it were just a simple mistake, someone would have fixed it by now. 

But someone in the system is actively changing or holding back parts of his results. I draw blood for a living, so I know what I saw on those initial screens. But... no matter how many doctors or family members I talk to, they just look at the altered chart and tell me the numbers are fine. It’s not a misunderstanding. It's intentional, and it’s just really wearing me down trying to get anyone to see what's actually happening.
Have you ever had similar concerns or beliefs in the past, where you felt strongly that something was happening that others didn't seem to notice or agree with?

No... no, not at all. I've never had any issues like this before. I'm just a regular person—I go to work, do my job, and come home. I've never felt like people were ignoring something obvious or that I had to fight to prove something like this. This is the first time anything like this has ever happened to me.
Have you ever had any other situations where you believed something was happening that others didn’t seem to notice or agree with, even if you couldn’t prove it?

Like I was just saying, no. There hasn't been anything else. It's really just this specific situation with my dad's chart. Before this started last year, I never had any reason to question things like this at work or in my life. I don't have a history of making things up, if that's what you mean. So, no, nothing else.
Are there any other things you believe are happening that most people wouldn’t agree with or understand—things that you just know are true even if you can’t prove them?

No. I mean, I really feel like you're asking me the same thing over and over. I don't have any other beliefs or... secrets or whatever you're looking for. It's just this one thing with my dad's medical records. That's it. I'm a normal person, I just want someone to look at the real lab results. There's nothing else going on.
Have you ever felt like people are watching you, following you, or trying to harm you in any way outside of this situation with your father's medical records?

No, I don't feel like anyone is watching me or following me. I've never felt like someone was trying to hurt me or anything like that. I really just go from my apartment to the clinic and back. It's just the records... that's the only thing that's wrong.

Can you tell me if, during this time of trying to prove your belief about your father's lab results, you've ever felt that something was happening that wasn't real—like seeing or hearing things that others couldn't, or believing something that no one else seems to understand?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. I mean, I work in a clinic, so I know what you're getting at with these questions, but... no. My senses are perfectly fine. I just know what I saw in those lab results, and that's real. But I'm definitely not hallucinating or imagining things, if that's what you're asking.
Have you ever had any beliefs that others find strange or irrational, but you were absolutely certain were true, even if you couldn't explain why?

No, I really haven't. I mean, I feel like we're just going in circles here. I don't have any strange beliefs or weird ideas. I just know what I saw in my dad's chart. That's the only thing. I don't have any other things going on that people would think are... irrational or whatever. Just the lab results.
